patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient reports a 2-month history of insidious onset left shoulder pain, worsening with extreme ranges of motion and activity. Pain disrupts sleep, and there's noted difficulty with activities of daily living like brushing hair and dressing. No history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, treated with metformin and glipizide.

Secondary_Symptoms: Difficulty sleeping on the affected side
Difficulty with brushing hair and dressing

patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with chronic left shoulder pain without a history of trauma.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: Doctor: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on? Patient: I’ve had a slow, worsening pain in my left shoulder for about two months. It hurts most when I try to move it to extreme positions or use it for activities like brushing my hair and dressing, and it often disrupts my sleep.

turns.doctor_question: I understand. To help me get a better picture of your current health, have you experienced any changes in your vision, such as blurriness, blind spots, or any loss of sight?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any changes in my vision—no blurriness, blind spots, or loss of sight.”

turns.doctor_question: To help me get a better picture of your overall health, could you tell me if you currently smoke or have a history of smoking?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I don’t smoke, and I’ve never smoked.”

turns.doctor_question: I understand. To help me get a better picture of how you're feeling, have you been experiencing any nausea or feeling sick to your stomach lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had nausea or felt sick to my stomach.”

turns.doctor_question: I understand. To help me get a better picture of your health, have you noticed any lumps or masses in your breast area that do not cause you any pain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any lumps or masses in my breast area, and nothing there has been painful.”

turns.doctor_question: I understand that physical symptoms can often be linked to how we are feeling overall. Lately, have you been experiencing a significant amount of psychological stress or emotional strain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t been experiencing significant psychological stress or emotional strain lately; the main issue has been the worsening left shoulder pain that makes it hard to brush my hair, dress, and it even wakes me up at night.”

turns.doctor_question: I understand. To help me get a better picture of your current health, could you tell me if you have noticed any changes in the color of your urine, specifically if it has appeared darker than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any change in the color of my urine—it hasn’t been darker than usual.”

turns.doctor_question: I understand that finding a change in your breast can be concerning. To help me better understand what you are experiencing, have you noticed if the mass has been growing or changing in size rapidly?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any breast lumps or masses at all, so I can’t say they’ve been growing or changing.”

turns.doctor_question: I'm sorry to hear you're not feeling well. To help me better understand what you're experiencing, could you please tell me if you are currently having any pain in your wrist?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I’m not having any pain in my wrist. My main problem is the left shoulder pain that’s worse with extreme movement and interferes with brushing my hair, dressing, and my sleep.”

turns.doctor_question: I understand. To help me get a clearer picture of what’s going on, could you please check your arms for me? Have you noticed any skin lesions, such as rashes, bumps, or marks, running along the path of your veins?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any rashes, bumps, or marks along the path of my veins on my arms. The only major issue I’m noticing is the worsening left shoulder pain, especially at extreme ranges of motion.”
